text: in one word amazing. i changed a couple of things, but my fiancee loved it! i used chicken breast, no beans (i don't like them), red pepper, green pepper, scallion, and instead of the two types of tomatoes i used one can of diced tomatoes, and one jar of medium salsa! i am looking forward to eating this for lunch all week. thanks for sharing!!!
best beef jerky recipe i've seen, turns out amazing.. thank you.
never made mushroom soup before, but this was beautiful. nice and creamy and flavourful, will make again as was so quick and easy to make. i didn't use the oil, just spray.
this recipe is, in actual fact, excellent but it's word for word lifted from best of the best of bridge, page 70, copyright august 1998, which also has loads of other terrific recipes.

just a basic, yummy, healthy soup. can't say it was hearty if made as written. it was brothy actually. loved the idea of doubling the carrots & corn.. (or just doubling all veggies). or instead, using 1 cup less broth. we served it with cheese toast.. pretty good! i think i will make it again.

excellent. i used 2 cups of carrots and 2 cups of celery instead of 1 cup. also used about 1 1/2 cup of onion. i like veggies so i went a little heavier on it. i used 8 corn tortillas rather than 10 to thicken the recipe. they really do disintegrate like the reviews said! everyone really loved it! finished it off with sour cream, tortilla strips fried, cheese, and cilantro. i also made sweet corn tamale cakes which were a nice addition.
soooo awesomely good!! goes great with chili, shephard's pie, etc.... moist and flavorful! easy to make! try it tonight!!!

this is the best split pea soup recipe i have ever tried. made it with an excellent left over easter ham a few weeks ago (used 1 tsp celery seed as i didn't have fresh celery) and it was fantastic. had to make it again. this time i didn't have a ham bone so i used a smoked pork neck (a lot cheaper than spiral cut ham - hocks could have been used as well) and it turned out just as good - obviously less protein this time though.

super recipe!!! i added extra mushrooms but did not have the pimiento or celery. it tasted great and the kids loved it. i also used bread crumbs mixed with melted butter and sprinkled on top. a super easy and fast recipe that will be in my meal rotation from now on!!! thanks kittencal!!
this is my favorite cornbread too. i don't know who thought of adding sugar in the first place....thanks for sticking to the basics.
took to family reunion - what a hit!

made this last night and it was so so so so so so so so good. hubby wants this at least once a week now. thank you for a great recipe, served this with potato pie recipe number 95345 and what a combo. thanks so much for a keeper recipe.
all i could taste was lime :(

i have made this a few times now. i use it if i am in a hurry. have tried rolling it out to use as well when i have a 2 layer pie but it is hard to handle. falls apart very easily. it has good flavor but is a very crumbly texture after baking. i will continue to use this for bottom crust only pies if i am in a pinch on time, but i prefer crust 28943 most incredible no fail pie crust for better flavor and texture.

this is a great, easy coffee recipe...works wonders for me because we are "between" coffee makers and this makes a nice rich brew without the equipment. i use more coffee (about 5 teaspoons)and usually more cinnamon, and less sugar ( i think it works well adjusting it to personal taste)...because of the sweetness of this blend i am able to drink it black...even iced - ( i'm usually a cream user!!!) wonderful for after dinner...a dessert all by itself! discovered during zwt3 and now a keeper for constant use!!! thank you elmotoo!!!

thanks tara! i used garlic powder, black pepper, and dried minced onion instead of the packet. i didn't want uncontrolled sodium, msg, soy, or other unnecessary chemicals. i used coconut oil, and romano cheese since that is made from sheeps milk, which is less processed than cows milk. turned out great!
best lemon drop martini ever! instead of super fine sugar, i use simple syrup

these were very nice! i normally use bread machine yeast in my maker but my husband had fortunately (i guess) bought active-dry this last time and i wasn't sure how these would turn out since i thought you were supposed to proof active-dry? anyway i just dumped it all in no proofing and these turned out excellent. i got 12 slider sized buns out of this with a bit of dough leftover so i just made 3 bonus rolls. the last few mins of baking i rubbed butter on the tops and sprinkled sesame seeds over, that was when they turned golden on top! sliced each one and these took our st. paddy's day guinness burgers http://www.food.com/recipe/guinness-burgers-22210 over the top! thanks!!

i made this using 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts and cooked for only 30 mins. this dish just seemed ok to me. instead of a honey butter sauce it tasted more like a sweet lemon sauce to me. it was very tart and tangy which i wasn't really expecting. don't think i would make this again, but it was worth trying.

this is very good. i browned the ground beef and drained off the grease. i also put a can of corn in it. my mom never made this but a friend's mother did when i was a kid and i loved it. she called it "goulash". i put some seasoning salt in it.
loved this recipe! the chicken was very moist and flavorful. i served it with rice and asparagus. my husband thought it was delicious, definitely a keeper!

ummm! used the dark rich version and highly recommend it. could have eaten the entire bowl with a spoon but managed to save some for the recipe #2496. suggest sifting cocoa and powdered sugar together. why buy the gross stuff in the can when this is so easy and uses ingredients you can pronounce? made for dh's birthday and will use again. thanks for sharing the recipe!

i did not have any trouble with this recipe. i was afraid of too much sesame oil taste so i only used 1 t in the sauce. i like the taste of fresh ginger so i added that to the sauce... it was very good. i did the 1/2 cup sugar instead of the 1 cup. the chicken cooked up well... i would do this recipe again. thanks.
followed the recipe exactly. everyone loves this potato salad. it's the only potato salad i will make!

help! i must step away from the pudding before it is all gone.. excellent recipe. used leftover jasmine rice.some half and half and a lot of cinnamon. i tempered the egg mixture before adding it to the pot just in case. shall definitely make again when there are others around to police me.

this recipe was very tasty. i served it for my husband and guests and everyone loved it. i used fresh oregano from my garden. next time (and there will definitely be a next time) i will use basil. i have to agree with one of the reviewers; it was a messy to make, but it was worth it. all-in-all, a great recipe!!!

i have never made country fried steak before but was willing to try since i got some cube steaks on sale at the grocery store. i made quite a mess while breading but it was well worth it! i browned the steaks for 4 minutes each side and they turned out really nice and crunchy and golden. i was not really thrilled with the gravy however, but that could have just been us. a great comfort meal that i served with mac n cheese and green beans. thanks for posting!!!

how is easy is this? chop up a bunch of vegetables and end up with a hearty and filling soup. my coworkers are all sick right now and i brought a quart of this into the office. lots of slurping and smiles. i doubled the oregano and otherwise followed the reicpe. thanks uncle bill.

this was great! loved the "bbq" sauce this made. very easy to throw together. with the leftover sauce i put it over some cooked chicken breast tenderloins and placed it in the frig. it was a fantastic snack. thanks denise for sharing this. can't wait to make it for the next potluck.
i made this for new years, and i swear, it was tasty and so easy. my husband loved it....thank you!

oh, my gosh! i am eating one of these warm out of the oven right now, and it is heavenly! they are super-moist, and certainly don't taste low-fat at all. i used whole-wheat flour and splenda instead of sugar, and they came out delightful. i really wanted a healthy banana muffin recipe, as i had three over-ripe bananas to use, but i decided i also wanted oats in them. thus, when i happened upon this recipe, i was delighted. they're exactly what i was looking for, and made a great dessert! thank you.

banana nut bread has to be one of my favorite things on earth, and to make one with leftover starter only makes it that much better. i use butter instead of shortening and white whole wheat flour, it rises beautifully and is absolutely yummy.
delicious! i didnt have cumin on hand, so omitted it. i had leftovers the next day, also great! served with steamed white rice.
i only made 1 c. of this dip but loved it. great with flipsides. still have leftovers after using it as an appetizer.

this was really good and super easy! i used chicken bullion and water for my chicken broth, so the only thing i would change next time is to not add the tsp of salt...i am sure it will be perfect! thanks for the great recipe!

i will make these again & again. so easy and fast. i skipped step 3 (letting the butter & herbs sit) because i was in a huge hurry. next time i may cut back on the cooking time a minute or two because these were a little crispy for our tastes. otherwise, excellent recipe - thank you!
very good. i omitted the red pepper flakes, but otherwise, better than my other attempts at brown rice. will make again.
love this kale! it is a fast and easy meal or side plus it is really yummy!

this was easy to make and delicious! i took it to my husband's work for the t-day potluck and it was the first thing gone!!! i added a little more pumpkin than it called for since i really like the taste of pumpkin. yum!
super marinade, i let it cool slightly and served it over a salad of baby greens with garden new potatoes on the side. this is a keeper.
truly an easy yet yummy recipe. we did however add sliced mushrooms as wine & chicken require it. highly recommend this for all ages. grandchildren loved it as well as the adults.

"wonderful, tasty, and glorious in it's ground-beefiness with a noble sweet tang. would recommend anyone who aspires to righteousness to partake of this holy meal." ~ this is my husband's review. now for mine. this was a very yummy meatloaf. i had one pound of beef and made 4 personal size meatloaves with it. i like the sauce also with the vinegar. i'm used to the ketchup/mustard/brown sugar type so this was a good change. i'll make this again!! thank you!
i made these today they were fantastic very easy to do,i had to bake them a little longer than suggested,i will be making this recipe often.
this is a winner. very easy to prepare. great flavor and texture. i only used 2 sticks of butter. i replaced the lemon juice with key lime juice

absolutely one of the best recipes i have tried. taste just like the local indian restaurant we have in our area. it was quick and easy i didn't have ginger paste; however, i did use about a tablespoon of powdered ginger.

this was quite good. very tender chicken. kids liked it although it was a little spicy for their taste due to the taco seasoning. hubby and i really liked the sweet/salty mix of it. definitely a good base for a lot of different variations.
this was delicious! it was a bit too tangy for my taste so i added a tablespoon of brown sugar and a teaspoon of baking soda. perfect!

yum! i made this with chicken breasts i had in the freezer, so i cut them up and cooked them first, then proceeded. i couldn't resist trowing in some peas, though! a very tasty recipe, thanks for posting! made for wt8
delicious and easy to prepare. i really love the onion in it. next time i will double up on that. thanks for posting.
lovely salad dressing...but you do have to watch what type of greens you mix it with! next time, i would cut the recipe in half

truly incredible! only thing i would change is not fully mixing the cheddar cubes and leaving them partially unmelted to create a bit more texture, and adding a bit of tabasco for kick. otherwise, it was exactly what i was looking for, and a perfect kick-off recipe for tweaking to personal tastes.

this was by far my favorite pizza dough recipe now. it had a great flavor and baked up nice and puffy. the dough did come out a little sticky and i had to add more flour, and i will take some others suggestion to pre-bake it in a hot oven before adding toppings next time because mine was slightly doughy in the center. it also made great breadsticks! thank you for posting!
awesome! i used regular mayo instead, and also added about 1/4 teaspoon of ground white pepper in the mix. perfect lunchtime food!

these are so amazing - i used flavored stuffing as well with the bush's vegetarian baked beans -- they were amazing -- definitely a keeper and i have been turning my friends on to them -- very flavorful as they are -- thanks for sharing

my partner and i loved this recipe! and like most people, i altered the recipe a bit. i cooked a whole chicken with a chopped onion, some whole peppercorns, a sprinkle of thyme, 1 tsp of celery salt and 1 tsp of salt, covering the entire thing in water. this made a lot of yummy broth, maybe too much. i didn't alter anything else. i will be making this again!
very yummy muffins. i used frozen raspberries, and these turned out great!
my family loved this, will make this again!!

what an impressive and great tasting side dish. so appealing and tastes terrific. made this with garden fresh vegetables and throughly enjoyed. definitely on the menu for upcoming long weekend in september! thank you merlot.

this made a super quick dinner! i doubled the sauce then tossed everything with some egg noodles. i might add a couple of garlic cloves and replace the green onions with shallots next time. yum! thanks mama's kitchen!
this is by far the best recipe for corn macque choux i have ever had! thid is my favorite way to eat corn. thanks for sharing this great recipe!!!!
superb breakfast casserole perfect for holiday breakfasts and company. i added a layer of sliced mushrooms on top of the other veggies. delicious! thanks for this great recipe!
saw the recipe and had to make it tonight. didn't change a thing, and it is delicious!

bravo! fantastic! we loved this, we will make this again, again and again i am sure. my husband has thanked me a hundred times and told me how great a meal it was. i served the chicken with refried beans, spanish rice, and soft tortilla.
i made this as is and it was delicious!! family requested to keep the recipe. a new family favorite! thanks for posting!
i made this last night and put it in the oven and it turned out perfectly. i think our only issue was we cut it so early it fell on one end but it didn't detract from the taste. outstanding!
a true new york style crumb cake. we love it! have made it a handful of times now. (and ps: the whole point of a ny style crumb is that it is loaded with topping)
very good! cooked from frozen and they turned out great!
i am not sure what happened but when i made these, the middle sunk and didn't cook through. it was really strange - i followed the directions exactly - no changes!!

my mom and i made this tonight... we could not believe how easy it was, and how much it tasted like real gyro meat! (we used 1/2 lamb, 1/2 beef -- the butcher had to grind the lamb for us at the store).

what a great low-carb recipe that doesn't taste low-carb! i made this yesterday with a couple changes. i used less splenda - about 1/4 cup and used apple cider vinegar instead of white vinegar. i think the longer this dish chills the better it tastes. the rest of my family who aren't carb restricted loved the taste too - i got lots of compliments. i think next time i will use even less splenda and maybe more spices, by just altering the sweet and spicy, you can really customize this one to your tastes.

these were really good. i made a few minor changes. i used oat bran instead of wheat, used honey instead of molasses because i didn't have molasses. i added ground flax meal and cut the oil down to 1/4 cup. also used fat free milk and added cinnamon. instead of raisins i used dates. really good recipe, the texture came out great.
first time i've had made it or even tasted it (for st. patrick's day 2007); really enjoyed it.
these are truly a taste of autumn. i made these as belgian waffles, served them topped with pecan maple butter and warmed maple syrup. these are a winner in our book.
these were delicious. the cheese made them so rich and creamy tasting.

this is 10 star all the way. next time i will not stir fry the meat as i couldn't get it crispy anyways, but the sauce is so fabulous that i can't wait to make it again. i must say that i only used 1 t fresh ginger, 2 cloves of garlic and 1 t. crushed red pepper. with these adustments it was perfect for us. thanks.
good but i don't think i made it right. i have to tweak it.
this recipe is awesome, so easy to make and such a hit with my family

this was easy and wonderful. only think i did different was use cheddar cheese on top. perfect everyone in my home loved it!!! i have cooked this before but never with basil and oregano and it makes a big difference!

i made this and it was very good. potatoes didn't cook as well as i hoped so i did throw the whole thing in the oven for 15 min on 350. next time i try this, i'm going to cook the potatoes first then add hot dogs.
will make again. thanks

i used two teaspoons of almond extract instead of vanilla to "up" the cherry flavor. i also rolled the warm cookies in confectioners sugar, twice. very good, quick and easy. thank you for posting the recipe, dib's.

this chicken is excellent. i have been making a roasted chicken of some kind every sabbath for the last few months (because i am teaching my sons to cook) we have made many lemon flavored chickens and this one is the best. made it as stated except an additional tablespoon each of butter and olive oil so we could also put some between the skin and breast and my chicken was much larger so we cooked it on 400° for the first hour and turned the temperature down to 350° to finish cooking. thanks for the great recipe. oh, it also browned beautifully! looked like it should be in a magazine. :)

this bread is delicious! i love the fact that it is not only extremely inexpensive to make, but it has the sweetness of store bought bread. i have been searching for that in the other recipes here, but even though they may have the texture i want they are quite bland. the whole family loves it! i made some toast with butter and strawberry jam and it was out of this world. thanks for sharing!

good cookies. i used natural, chunky peanut butter (makes great cookies!) you don't need to use the processed sweetened varieties to make a good peanut butter cookie. i also added 1/2 teaspoon of salt and two teaspoons of vanilla. they came out great this way. not too sweet, but rich, crunchy, chewy and delicious all at the same time! 4 stars because cookies need salt and vanilla in my opinion. other than that, a good recipe for sure!!! thanks heather
delicious! made just as written except i used regular flour and salted the chicken before coating it in the flour.

great meal for very little effort. we are renovating our kitchen so crockpot meals are perfect. i served the meal with a side of honey-glazed carrots. i think my family will ask for this...even after the new kitchen is in!
the best chocolate chip cookie, oh my goodness! i don't modify the recipe at all.

this was really good. i added green peppers, onion, mushrooms, fresh garlic, italian seasoning, and used a penne pasta. i did find it took closer to 45-50 minutes to finish. the cream cheese layers add a lot to this. thank you for posting a recipe i will use again!

the lemon baked cod is delicious! i was in a hurry to fix dinner and found this recipe. it takes only a few minutes to put together and by the time i made a salad, cooked vegetables and set the table, the lemon baked cod was ready! my husband and i loved it!

these cookies were good but i don't think the dough was sweet enough for my taste, and it was a little on the dry side. i used snickers, rolos and peanut butter cups for the candy in mine. the photo is with rolos i believe. with all the rave reviews i have to say i was a little disappointed with the end result. thank you for sharing your recipe with us angelcakes. linda

mmmmmm...this is got to be the best banana bread recipe ever! i had found one previously that was pretty good...but i didn't have any creme de freshe that the recipe called for. so i can online to look for a good recipe...and i think i've found it!! uses all the basic ingredients, but the results are incredible! the only thinkthat i did differently was use brown sugar instead of white sugar. but just remeber that if you are using overly ripe bananas...like i did, minimize the amount of sugar because it was a bit too sweet. other than that, theres no complaints from me! tomorrow i am going to be making four loaves. two to keep at home and two to bring to a party/potluck thing i am going to!! definately a keeper! :)
we enjoyed these today at a party hosted by another zaar member and they are absolutely scrumptious! they will be on the menu for my next party!
this recipe was a big hit! i used fresh morzerella in it but otherwise followed the recipe....
made for the super bowl.... didn't last long!

i have gotten addicted to this recipe! i have made it a lot already and have tried several alterations, all of which work out great: add 1 t. cinnamon, add 1/2 c. shredded coconut, substitute 1 c. ground flax seeds or pumpkin seeds for the pecans, substitute 4 c. cheerios instead of 2 c. of oats (i ran out). my next experiment is to add a small amount of ginger powder and about 1/3 c. minced candied ginger... thanks for sharing this "keeper"!

this is amazing! easy to make and fantastic tasting. love that you saute the toppings. it makes the flavors blend and it truly comes together well. we have already made it twice and are planning a white pizza next time. yum!!!
has anyone tried a savoury variation of this? it would be good to have a low carb/low gi replacement for bread to enjoy with soup.

this is a great way to fix broccoli. i used fresh broccoli crowns which were separated into flowerets, rinsed and put in a microwave safe dish. i did not add the water and the garlic was thinly sliced and cooked along with the broccoli. i reduced the oil to 1 tablespoon, lightly sprinkled the dish with salt and used 1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes. something i know i will do again.

i had never fixed a tri-tip before but several good friends rave about them on a weekly basis. i got a 2.5 lb at the store and followed this recipe exactly. we didn't find one thing to complain about. next time i will let it sit an entire day (or two). grilled for 8 minutes on each side for the perfect medium rare we so love. meat was flavorful, juicy and tender. thanks for making my first attempt at fixing this cut of meat a huge success!
one of the best recipes i have made with simply potatoes
